This kinase is known to be a target of Claulansine D, a compound that has been shown to modulate cellular processes through its interaction with the kinase. The presence of a direct target relationship between Claulansine D and A-431 implies that the compound may exert its effects through the modulation of this kinase. The integration of these pathways suggests that Viscidulin Iii could act as a modulator of the cAMP pathway, potentially influencing the activity of Claulansine D and thereby affecting the function of A-431. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Viscidulin Iii and A-431, though further experimental validation is required to confirm the specific interactions and biological relevance.
